item.text: I have enough behavior mapped to code it cleanly. I’m creating a small local IDNA library now: manual `argparse`-style parsing, a pure JS Bootstring encoder/decoder, Unicode validation/remap helpers, and the `/output/test3.mjs` entrypoint that preserves Python’s output quirks.

The first pass of the modules is in place. I’m running the Node entrypoint against the executable on the sample cases and the tricky parser/error cases now, then I’ll patch any mismatches instead of assuming the port is correct.

/bin/bash -c 'tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
run_case() {
  name=$1
  shift
  /workspace/dataset/test3_executable "$@" >"$tmpdir/${name}.py.out" 2>"$tmpdir/${name}.py.err"
  py_rc=$?
  node /output/test3.mjs "$@" >"$tmpdir/${name}.js.out" 2>"$tmpdir/${name}.js.err"
  js_rc=$?
  printf '"'CASE:%s\\n' \""'$name"
  printf '"'PY_RC:%s JS_RC:%s\\n' \""'$py_rc" "$js_rc"
  diff -u "$tmpdir/${name}.py.out" "$tmpdir/${name}.js.out" || true
  diff -u "$tmpdir/${name}.py.err" "$tmpdir/${name}.js.err" || true
}
